findings.title: Missed conversion of scale-color($primary) in categories badge-notification
findings.body: In `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification`, the color is still `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` and was not converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` like every other identical `$lightness: 50%` usage in this same file (lines 48, 51, 55, 69, 246, 301). This PR's whole purpose is to fix dark-theme contrast for scale-color($primary) usages; this spot was overlooked, so the badge-notification text color on category topic lists will remain unreadable/low-contrast on dark themes.

findings.title: Lightness values swapped when converting .topic-meta-data h5 a color
findings.body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. Following the pattern used everywhere else in this PR, the correct conversion should preserve 30% for the primary branch and use the complementary 70% for secondary, i.e. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. Instead the primary branch lightness was changed to 70% (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`), which produces a much lighter color than before for the default/light theme, likely reducing readability of this anchor text against the light background. This is inconsistent with the symmetric X/(100-X) pattern used consistently elsewhere in the diff.

findings.title: Lost original lightness value when converting .group-member-info .name color
findings.body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The converted rule became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, i.e. identical to the sibling `.title` rule a few lines below instead of preserving the original 30%/70% pair. This changes the visual appearance of usernames in the group-member-info block (now lighter/less contrasted than before) and appears to be a copy-paste mistake rather than an intentional change.

findings.title: Same incorrect lightness substitution as desktop/user.scss for .group-member-info .name
findings.body: Mirroring the desktop version, the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` instead of the expected 30%/70% complementary pair, duplicating the same mistake across the mobile stylesheet and causing an unintended contrast change for usernames in group listings on mobile.

findings.title: Incorrect lightness mapping for .topic-map h3 color
findings.body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` (a fairly dark color). It was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` rather than preserving the 20%/80% complementary pair used by the sibling `.number, i` rule a few lines below (which correctly became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`). This makes the topic-map header text noticeably lighter than intended on the default theme.

findings.title: Primary/secondary lightness values swapped for .custom-message-length
findings.body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The converted rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which changes the primary-branch lightness from 70% to 30% instead of keeping 70%/30% as the complementary pair (consistent with the desktop version of this same rule in desktop/modal.scss, which correctly produced `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`). This introduces a noticeably darker text color for `.custom-message-length` on the default/light theme than existed before this PR.
